question.text:
The disjoint union $A_1 \sqcup A_2 \sqcup A_3$ of events $A_1,A_2,A_3$ covers the entire sample space. Compute $P(A_2|B)$ given the following probabilities:

\begin{align*} & P(B|A_1)=0.4, & P(A_1) = 0.2 \\[3pt] & P(B|A_2)=0.5, & P(A_2)=0.3 \\[3pt] & P(B|A_3)=0.3, &P(A_3)=0.5 \\[3pt] \end{align*}

Round your answer to $3$ decimal places.
question.explanation:
If the disjoint union $A_1 \sqcup A_2 \sqcup \ldots \sqcup A_n$ covers the entire sample space, Bayes' theorem combined with the law of total probability gives us the following:

\[ P(A_k | B) = \dfrac{P(B|A_k) P(A_k)}{P(B)} = \dfrac{P(B|A_k) P(A_k)}{\sum_{i=1}^n P(B|A_i)P(A_i)} \]

where $k=1,2,\ldots,n.$

In our case, $n=3,$ and $A_1 \sqcup A_2 \sqcup A_3$ covers the entire sample space. Consequently, we have

\[ P(A_1) + P(A_2) + P(A_3) = 0.2+0.3+0.5 = 1. \]

Therefore, we have

\begin{align*} P(A_2 | B) &= \dfrac{P(B|A_2) P(A_2)}{\sum_{i=1}^3 P(B|A_i)P(A_i)} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{P(B|A_2) P(A_2)}{P(B|A_1)P(A_1) + P(B|A_2)P(A_2) + P(B|A_3)P(A_3)} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{(0.5) (0.3)}{(0.4)(0.2) + (0.5)(0.3) + (0.3)(0.5)} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{0.15}{0.38} \\[5pt] &\approx 0.395, \end{align*}

rounded to $3$ decimal places.

example.title: Computing a Conditional Probability Using Bayes' Theorem

question.text:
A manufacturing company has three sites, factory $1,$ factory $2,$ and factory $3.$ They all produce two light bulb types: A and B.

  • Factory $1$ produces $25\%$ of the entire production, and $2\%$ of those bulbs are defective.
  • Factory $2$ produces $50\%$ of the entire production, and $3\%$ of those bulbs are defective.
  • Factory $3$ produces $25\%$ of the entire production, and $1\%$ of those bulbs are defective.

If $40\%$ of all light bulbs are of type A, and $1\%$ of type A light bulbs are defective, what is the probability that a randomly chosen defective light bulb is of type A? Round your answer to $3$ decimal places.
question.explanation:
Let $A$ be the event that a light bulb is of type A, $D$ be the event that a light bulb is defective, and $F_1, F_2, F_3$ be the event that a light bulb is produced in factory $1,$ $2,$ or $3,$ respectively.

Let's break down the information given in the problem statement:

  • From the bullet points, we have the following information: \begin{align*} & P(F_1) = 0.25 && P(D | F_1) = 0.02 \\[3pt] & P(F_2) = 0.5 && P(D | F_2) = 0.03 \\[3pt] & P(F_3) = 0.25 && P(D | F_3) = 0.01 \end{align*} The disjoint union $F_1 \sqcup F_2 \sqcup F_3$ covers the entire sample space, and we have \[ P(F_1)+ P(F_2) + P(F_3) = 0.25+0.5+0.25 = 1. \]

  • Since $40\%$ of all light bulbs are of type A, we have \[ P(A) = 0.4. \]

  • Since $1\%$ of type A light bulbs are defective, we have \[ P(D | A) = 0.01. \]

We want to find the probability that a randomly chosen defective light bulb is of type A, which is represented as $P(A | D).$

Using Bayes' theorem combined with the law of total probability, we have

\begin{align*} P(A | D) &= \dfrac{P(D | A) P(A)}{P(D)} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{P(D | A) P(A) }{P(D | F_1) P(F_1) + P(D | F_2) P(F_2) + P(D | F_3) P(F_3)} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{ (0.01)(0.4) }{ (0.02)(0.25) + (0.03)(0.5) + (0.01)(0.25)} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{0.004}{0.0225} \\[5pt] &\approx 0.178, \end{align*}

rounded to $3$ decimal places.

example.title: Applying Bayes’ Theorem to a Situation in Context

question.text:
In a nature park, there are $4$ species of squirrels, each with the same population.

  • Among the squirrels of species $1,$ $12\%$ are born in captivity.
  • Among the squirrels of species $2,$ $5\%$ are born in captivity.
  • Among the squirrels of species $3,$ $6\%$ are born in captivity.
  • Among the squirrels of species $4,$ $3\%$ are born in captivity.

If $35\%$ of the squirrels are adult females, and $8\%$ of the adult female squirrels are born in captivity, what is the probability that a randomly chosen squirrel born in captivity is an adult female? Round your answer to $3$ decimal places.
question.explanation:
Let $F$ be the event that a squirrel is an adult female, $C$ be the event that a squirrel is born in captivity, and $S_1, S_2, S_3, S_4$ be the event that a squirrel is of species $1,$ $2,$ $3,$ or $4,$ respectively.

Let's break down the information given in the problem statement:

  • Each species has the same number of squirrels, so we have the following information: \begin{align*} P(S_1) = P(S_2) = P(S_3) = P(S_4) = 0.25 \end{align*}

  • From the bullet points, we have the following information: \begin{align*} & P(C | S_1) = 0.12 \\[3pt] & P(C | S_2) = 0.05 \\[3pt] & P(C | S_3) = 0.06 \\[3pt] & P(C | S_4) = 0.03 \end{align*} The disjoint union $S_1 \sqcup S_2 \sqcup S_3 \sqcup S_4$ covers the entire sample space, and we have \[ P(S_1)+ P(S_2) + P(S_3) + P(S_4) = 0.25+0.25+0.25 +0.25 = 1. \]

  • Since $35\%$ of the squirrels are adult females, we have \[ P(F) = 0.35. \]

  • Since $8\%$ of adult females are born in captivity, we have \[ P(C | F) = 0.08. \]

We want to find the probability that a randomly chosen squirrel born in captivity is an adult female, which is represented as $P(F | C).$

Using Bayes' theorem combined with the law of total probability, we have

\begin{align*} P(F | C) &= \dfrac{P(C | F) P(F)}{P(C)} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{P(C | F) P(F) }{P(C | S_1) P(S_1) + P(C | S_2) P(S_2) + P(C | S_3) P(S_3) + P(C | S_3) P(S_3)} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{ (0.08)(0.35) }{ (0.12)(0.25) + (0.05)(0.25) + (0.06)(0.25) + (0.03)(0.25)} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{0.028}{0.065} \\[5pt] &\approx 0.431, \end{align*}

rounded to $3$ decimal places.

example.title: Applying Bayes’ Theorem to a Situation in Context

question.text:
In a nature park, there are $4$ species of squirrels, species $1$, species $2$, species $3,$ and species $4.$ Each species has the same population.

  • $8\%$ of squirrels of species $1$ are born in captivity.
  • $9\%$ of squirrels of species $2$ are born in captivity.
  • $11\%$ of squirrels of species $4$ are born in captivity.

If $42\%$ of the squirrels are adult females, $8\%$ of the adult female squirrels are born in captivity, and $36\%$ of the squirrels born in captivity are adult females, what is the probability that a randomly chosen squirrel from species $3$ is born in captivity? Round your answer to $3$ decimal places.
question.explanation:
Let $F$ be the event that a squirrel is an adult female, $C$ be the event that a squirrel is born in captivity, and $S_1, S_2, S_3, S_4$ be the event that a squirrel is of species $1,$ $2,$ $3,$ or $4,$ respectively.

Let's break down the information given in the problem statement:

  • Each species has the same number of individuals, so we have the following information: \begin{align*} P(S_1) = P(S_2) = P(S_3) = P(S_4) = 0.25 \end{align*}

  • From the bullet points, we have the following information: \begin{align*} & P(C | S_1) = 0.08 \\[3pt] & P(C | S_2) = 0.09 \\[3pt] & P(C | S_4) = 0.11 \end{align*} The disjoint union $S_1 \sqcup S_2 \sqcup S_3 \sqcup S_4$ covers the entire sample space, and we have \[ P(S_1)+ P(S_2) + P(S_3) + P(S_4) = 0.25+0.25+0.25 +0.25 = 1. \]

  • Since $42\%$ of the squirrels are adult females, we have \[ P(F) = 0.42. \]

  • Since $8\%$ of adult females are born in captivity, we have \[ P(C | F) = 0.08. \]

  • Since $36\%$ of squirrels born in captivity are adult females, we have \[ P(F | C) = 0.36. \]

We want to find the probability that a randomly chosen squirrel from species $3$ is born in captivity, which is represented as $P(C | S_3).$

Using Bayes' theorem combined with the law of total probability, we have

\begin{align*} P(F | C) &= \dfrac{P(C | F) P(F)}{P(C)} \\[5pt] 0.36 &= \dfrac{P(C | F) P(F) }{P(C | S_1) P(S_1) + P(C | S_2) P(S_2) + P(C | S_3) P(S_3) + P(C | S_4) P(S_4)} \\[5pt] 0.36 &= \dfrac{ (0.08)(0.42) }{ (0.08)(0.25) + (0.09)(0.25) + P(C | S_3)(0.25) + (0.11)(0.25)} \\[5pt] 0.36 &= \dfrac{ 0.0336 }{ 0.07 + 0.25P(C | S_3)}. \end{align*}

Solving this equation for $P(C | S_3),$ we have

\begin{align*} 0.36(0.07 + 0.25P(C | S_3))&= 0.0336 \\[5pt] 0.07 + 0.25P(C | S_3)&= \dfrac{0.0336}{0.36} \\[5pt] 0.07 + 0.25P(C | S_3)&= \dfrac{7}{75} \\[5pt] 0.25P(C | S_3) &= \dfrac{7}{75} - 0.07 \\[5pt] P(C | S_3) &= \dfrac{1}{0.25}\left(\dfrac{7}{75} - 0.07 \right) \\[5pt] P(C | S_3) &\approx 0.093 \end{align*}

rounded to three decimal places.

example.title: Solving for an Unknown Conditional Probability

question.text:
A farm sells its apples to three grocery stores; $1,$ $2,$ and $3.$

  • Store $1$ buys $14\%$ of the apples.
  • Store $2$ buys $26\%$ of the apples, and $50\%$ of those apples are sold in one day.
  • Store $3$ buys $60\%$ of the apples, and $25\%$ of those apples are sold in one day.

If $63\%$ of all apples are red, $25\%$ of red apples are sold in one day, and $45\%$ of apples sold in one day are red, what is the probability that a randomly chosen apple bought by store $1$ is sold in one day? Round your answer to $1$ decimal place.
question.explanation:
Let $R$ be the event that an apple is red, $S$ be the event that the apple is sold in one day, and $S_1, S_2, S_3$ be the event that an apple is sold by store $1,$ $2,$ or $3,$ respectively.

Let's break down the information given in the problem statement:

  • From the bullet points, we have the following information: \begin{align*} & P(S_1) = 0.14 \\[3pt] & P(S_2) = 0.26 && P(S | S_2) = 0.5 \\[3pt] & P(S_3) = 0.60 && P(S | S_3) = 0.25 \end{align*} The disjoint union $S_1 \sqcup S_2 \sqcup S_3$ covers the entire sample space, and we have \[ P(S_1)+ P(S_2) + P(S_3) = 0.14+0.26+0.60 = 1. \]

  • Since $63\%$ of all apples are red, we have \[ P(R) = 0.63. \]

  • Since $25\%$ of red apples are sold in one day, we have \[ P(S | R) = 0.25. \]

  • Since $45\%$ of apples sold in one day are red, we have \[ P(R | S) = 0.45. \]

We want to find the probability that a randomly chosen apple bought by store $1$ is sold in one day, which is represented as $P(S | S_3).$

Using Bayes' theorem combined with the law of total probability, we have

\begin{align*} P(R | S) &= \dfrac{P(S | R) P(R)}{P(S)} \\[5pt] P(R | S) &= \dfrac{P(S | R) P(R) }{P(S | S_1) P(S_1) + P(S | S_2) P(S_2) + P(S | S_3) P(S_3)} \\[5pt] 0.45 &= \dfrac{ (0.63)(0.25) }{ P(S | S_1)(0.14) + (0.5)(0.26) + (0.25)(0.60)} \\[5pt] 0.45 &= \dfrac{0.1575}{0.14P(S | S_1) + 0.28} \\[5pt] \end{align*}

Solving this equation for $P(S | S_1),$ we have

\begin{align*} 0.45(0.14P(S | S_1) + 0.28)&= 0.1575 \\[5pt] 0.14P(S | S_1) + 0.28 &= \dfrac{0.1575}{0.45} \\[5pt] 0.14P(S | S_1) + 0.28 &= 0.35 \\[5pt] 0.14P(S | S_1) &= 0.35 - 0.28\\[5pt] 0.14P(S | S_1) &= 0.07\\[5pt] P(S | S_1)&= \dfrac{0.07}{0.14}\\[5pt] P(S | S_1)&= 0.5. \end{align*}
